short: Route groups, one policy zone each
is: Route groups split along the DESIGN subdomain→namespace→router seam, each an independently mounted policy zone.
conventions: Each module exposes exactly one `*_router()`; adding a domain = a new module + one line in `app()`.
This split is the intermediate step toward per-domain crates — extraction should be a move, not a redesign.
`accounts.rs` handlers call `application::account::*` use cases and project the result to the generated wire type; no use-case logic lives in the handler.
entry_points: mod.rs (the group index + the CSRF layer)

fs.name: accounts.rs
fs.role: account/membership/invitation JSON API; thin driver: CallingUser → application::account::* → wire projection (ZMVP-205)

fs.name: commissions/
fs.role: the commission JSON API, one file per act

fs.name: mod.rs
fs.role: group index + require_first_party_origin CSRF middleware (an Origin header must equal public_url's origin; an opaque origin matches nothing)

fs.name: session.rs
fs.role: browser sign-in: POST /signin (sets the browser-binding cookie), GET /signin-callback (hands that cookie to complete; clears it only when the authenticator proved it matched, decided on its own answer before provisioning: an accepted browser — success, or either 500 after it (provisioning, session write) — or account_mismatch, SignInFailure::matched_the_binding; every other answer leaves it to expire, or the next sign-in replaces it), GET /me, POST /logout; every redirect a Url built on Config::public_url, failures as the closed SignInFailure codes (denied, invalid_callback, exchange_failed, account_mismatch, browser_mismatch)

refs.title: Actor Addressing — DID as the Only Identifier, Everywhere
refs.governs: `accounts.rs` — Account addressed by DID, no surrogate id

notes: `PATCH /accounts/{id}/handle`: DID-doc-first ordering — the did:plc UPDATE-op lands before the private-store write (DD 27852802).
`wellknown.rs`'s namespace-membership check and `application::account`'s claim checks share one parsed `HandleDomain`, so they can never disagree on the namespace.
